title: Mapping of domain-mediated protein-protein interaction by SPOT peptide assay
protocol: Switch on the peptide synthesizer and its accessories, then start the instrument-controlling computer.
Run the peptide synthesis software on the computer.
Open the peptide sequence file in the “Edit sequence” function of the software.
Transform the peptide sequence into the proper format readable by MultiPep.
Enter the protein name.
Perform a ‘peptide walk’.
Type the length of peptides and number of overlaps between subsequent peptides (e.g., ".seq, 20,2").
Give the order to insert a single space between spots if needed.
Command the instrument to leave the remaining row after your last peptide vacant with “.newline.”.
Enter “.end” to command the instrument to stop the peptide spot.
Calibrate and assemble the 1 mL syringe and the spotter needle.
Prime the two dilutors to get rid of air bubbles by pressing the prime button five times.
Pipette prepared aa derivatives into MultiPep 1 tubes in the fume hood.
Mount the membrane on the device frame properly in the fume hood, ensuring no bubble or wrinkle is introduced.
Wash the membrane in ethanol thrice.
Run the synthesis using the MultiPep 1 machine according to specified parameters.
Decap reagents consisting of 1.1 M DIC, 1.1 M HOBt⋅H2O, 5% acetic anhydride solutions, and 20% piperidine.
Mount all reagents in correct points on the substance stand of MultiPep 1 machine.
Place aa cylinders/tubes into specified points on the stand.
Remove caps from amino acid cylinders/tubes before loading them into the stand.
Unlid 0.5 mL micro-centrifuge tubes and load them into holders beside the amino acid tubes.
Mix activator with amino acids in a 3:2 ratio within the mixing tubes.
Press the START button under “Run Synthesis” tab to initiate peptide synthesis.
Check the reaction during the first cycle to ensure spotting is running well.
Pause synthesis by pressing the PAUSE button if reagents need replenishment, ensuring the needle is disengaged from the reagent stand and aa tubes.
Replenish reagents as needed during pauses between deprotection steps.
Discard all remaining reagents in proper waste containers upon completion of synthesis.
Collect waste according to institutional hazardous waste rules.
Connect a carboy to the synthesizer equipment during peptide synthesis.
Mark corners of the membrane and other positions to be cut with a pencil once synthesis is finished.
Take out the membrane and put it in a single solvent-resistant container slightly larger than the membrane.
Use 20 mL dH2O to wash the membrane thrice for 5 min on a shaker.
Incubate the membrane in 0.02% bromophenol blue solution with gentle shaking at 20°C‒25°C for about 1 h.
Rinse the membrane with dH2O until background disappears.
Wash the membrane with ethanol and air-dry it at 20°C‒25°C.
Use a pencil to draw a grid on the membrane which encircles each spot location.
Transfer the membrane into a container labeled TFA in the fume hood.
Incubate the membrane in 15 mL of deprotection solution for 1.5 h, covering the container with a lid and agitating it every 15 min.
Wash the membrane in 30 mL dichloromethane (DCM) four times for 10 min each.
Wash the membrane in 30 mL DMF four times for 2 min each.
Wash the membrane in 30 mL ethanol twice for 2 min each.
Dilute 24 μg of plasmid in 1.5 mL of Opti-MEM I medium.
Mix gently.
Dilute 60 μL of Lipofectamine 2000 in 1.5 mL of Opti-MEM I medium.
Mix thoroughly by inverting the tube.
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Combine the Lipofectamine and DNA solutions (total volume is 3 mL).
Mix gently by slowly inverting the tube.
Incubate the solution for 20 minutes at 20°C‒25°C.
Add the 3.0 mL of DNA-Lipofectamine solution to cell cultures.
Gently agitate the dish to dispense the complex evenly over the cells.
Place the dishes at 37°C in the CO2 incubator for 24–48 hours.
Wash cells by removing the medium and rinsing twice with PBS buffer.
Add 2.5 mL Trypsin for cell dissociation and incubate the cells for 5 min at 37°C in the CO2 incubator.
Add 7.5 mL medium to deactivate trypsin and gently dissociate cells by pipetting.
Move cells to a 50 mL falcon.
Centrifuge at 1000 rpm for 5 min.
Rinse with PBS twice.
Add 1–1.5 mL lysis buffer with protease inhibitor.
Sonicate the cell lysate (50% duty cycles, 5 output control, 3 pulsed).
Place the lysates on a shaker with agitation for 15–30 min.
Centrifuge the lysates for 10 min at 12000 × g.
Move the supernatant to a tube on ice.
Filter lysates using a 0.45 μm strainer if clumped cells are present.
Save 1/30 volume of the lysate for testing expression of FLAG fusion protein by Western blotting or coomassie blue analysis.
Affinity-immunoprecipitate FLAG-fused proteins using FLAG-M2 antibody and coupled affinity gel.
Rinse an empty column with 1× washing buffer.
Load 0.8 mL of anti-FLAG M2 affinity gel on the column.
Suspend the resin thoroughly to achieve a homogeneous suspension, using a 2:1 proportion of the suspension to packed gel volume.
Elute immunoprecipitated FLAG-fused proteins from the resin with acidic buffer or by competition with the FLAG peptide.
Concentrate purified proteins to remove solvents and undesirable molecules.
Include a positive control reaction with a known FLAG-tagged protein.
Include a negative control reaction with an un-transfected sample.
Spin the resin for 30 s at 5000–8200 × g.
Discard the flow-through.
Rinse the column with 1 mL of washing buffer and centrifuge to remove wash solutions.
Wash the column with 1 mL of elution buffer, repeating three times, allowing each milliliter to pass through before adding the next.
Pass 10 mL of washing buffer through the column, pipetting beads up and down to accelerate flow.
Add cell lysate to the washed resin.
Agitate the sample gently on a shaker for 2 h.
Wash the beads with at least 3 column volumes of ice-cold washing buffer.
Collect the washing buffer that has passed through the column for Western blotting or coomassie blue analysis.
Elute the proteins with 3× 2 mL of elution buffer.
Incubate the sample at 20°C‒25°C with gentle shaking for 5 min.
Centrifuge the resin for 30 s at 5000–8200 × g.
Allow the beads to drain between each addition and collect 1 mL fractions in separate tubes which contain 50 μL of 1 M Tris (pH 8).
Prepare 3× FLAG elution buffer by mixing 180 μL of 5 μg/μL 3× FLAG peptide solution with 6 mL of 1× wash buffer to make a final concentration of 150 ng/mL.
Add 6 × 1 mL of 3× FLAG elution buffer to the resin.
Incubate the sample for 30 min at 4°C with gentle shaking.
Collect fractions by centrifuging the resin for 30 s at 5000–8200 × g.
Wash the beads with 2 column volumes of elution buffer, pipetting the beads up and down to accelerate the process.
Neutralize the beads with 2 column volumes of PBS.
Add sodium azide (to 0.1% v/v final concentration) directly to the PBS in the column for long term storage.
Seal the column and store at 4°C.
Save 20 μL samples of eluted fractions for blotting and Coomassie blue staining.
Add 10–50 μg of lysates or purified protein into 12 μL total volume of Non-Reducing Sample Buffer to prepare blotting samples.
Load samples in SDS-PAGE gel (7.5%–12%).
Run SDS-PAGE as standard protocol for blotting.
Move the gel into a staining box containing Coomassie staining buffer after completing the SDS-PAGE running.
Incubate the gel in the buffer with slow shaking for 2 h.
Pour off the Coomassie staining buffer into a bottle marked "Used Coomassie staining buffer".
Add appropriate amount of Coomassie destaining buffer to completely cover the gel and incubate the gel with slow shaking until protein bands are visible.
Pool the eluted fractions containing FLAG tagged protein as detected by Western blot analysis.
Place the pooled fractions in a Vivaspin centrifugal concentrator filled to maximum volume.
Centrifuge for 30 min at 1000 × g.
Empty the filtrate container.
Refill the concentrator using fresh buffer to make concentrate back up to original volume.
Centrifuge again as before.
Empty the filtrate container.
Repeat the process to achieve a considerable reduction in the concentration of contaminating microsolute.
Transfer the concentrated, de-salted sample from the bottom of the concentrate pocket to new tubes.
Keep the sample on ice.
Incubate membrane containing synthesized JMJD3/Kdm6b peptides with a mixture of purified Flag-BAF155 and Flag-BAF170 proteins for 16 hours.
Wash the membrane.
Expose the membrane to anti-Flag antibody.
Apply HRP-conjugated secondary antibody.
Scan peptides on membranes using enhanced chemiluminescence (ECL) reagents for interaction between BAF155/BAF170 and synthesized peptides.
Soak the membrane in about 5‒10 mL of methanol for 5‒10 minutes.
Rinse the membrane with TBST with four times shaking for 5 min each.
Block the membrane with the prepared blocking solution for 1 h at 20°C‒25°C.
Move the membrane into new blocking, containing 5 μg/mL of purified Flag-BAF155 and Flag-BAF170 protein solution and incubate it for 16 h at 4°C.
Rinse the membrane with TBST with shaking for four times, 5 min each.
Incubate the blocked membrane with anti-Flag primary antibody in blocking solution at a dilution of 1:1000 for 16 h at 4°C.
Rinse the membrane with TBST with shaking for four times, 5 min each.
Incubate the membrane in blocking solution containing HRP-conjugated secondary antibody at a dilution of 1:5000 at 20°C‒25°C rocking for 1‒2 h.
Rinse the membrane with TBST with shacking for four times, 10‒15 min each.
Detect signals of HRP reaction using ECL Plus detection reagents.
Cover the membrane with 1 mL of SuperSignal west substrate solution and incubate for 1 min.
Place the X-ray film against the membrane in a light-proof cassette.
Expose the X-ray film for an appropriate time period from 15 seconds to 10 minutes.
Develop the X-ray film with an X-ray film developer.
Strip the membrane if detection of protein-peptide binding by anti-Flag primary antibody causes high background or low signal.
Incubate the stripped membrane with either anti-BAF155 or anti-BAF170 antibody at a dilution of 1:200.
Wet the membrane with TBST solution if it is not directly used in the next experiment.
Store the wetted membrane in a heat-sealed polyester bag at 2°C to 8°C to prevent drying.
Incubate membrane in 1× stripping buffer I with gentle shaking for 10‒15 minutes at 20°C‒25°C.
Add an equal volume of 1× blocking buffer.
Wash blots two times for 5 minutes each with PBS.

Check the success of the stripping by exposing the membrane with ECL Plus detection reagents and with X-ray film for about 10 minutes to confirm complete removal of transiently interacting protein and bound antibodies.
Re-block for 10 minutes with 5% milk in PBS.
Rinse the membrane thrice with ddH2O for 10 minutes each.
Rinse the membrane with stripping buffer II at least four times for 30 minutes at 50°C.
Wash the membrane with 10× PBS at least three times for 20 minutes each at 20°C‒25°C.
Wash the membrane thrice for 20 minutes each with TBST at 20°C‒25°C.
Wash the membrane thrice for 10 minutes each with TBS at 20°C‒25°C.

Check the success of the stripping by exposing the membrane with ECL Plus detection reagents and with X-ray film for about 10 min to confirm the complete removal of transiently interacting protein and bound antibodies.
Rinse the membrane with ddH2O twice for 10 min each if signal is still observed.
Incubate the membrane with stripping buffer IIIA three times for 10 min each.
Incubate the membrane with stripping buffer IIIB three times for 10 min each.
Rinse the membrane with ddH2O twice for 10 min each.
Wash the membrane with TBST three times for 10 min each.

Check the success of the stripping by exposing the membrane with ECL Plus detection reagents and with X-ray film for about 10 min to confirm the complete removal of transiently interacting protein and bound antibodies.
